local_attempt.outcome: SIGN CONTRADICTION — confidently reported, passes its own refutation checks
local_attempt.note: Local's ATE is -0.1973, reported as 'a statistically significant reduction in homicide rates' — the OPPOSITE sign from both the published finding (Cheng & Hoekstra 2013: laws INCREASE homicide ~8%) and GADS's own cloud reference run on this identical spec (+0.1057). Placebo (0.0163) and subset (-0.1939) refutation checks both 'passed,' lending false confidence — those checks validate specification robustness, not whether the sign/direction is right. This is the second instance in this local-mode pass (after prop99_cigarette_sales) of a confidently-wrong, refutation-checked result with no visible warning sign. See notes.md.

estimate.note: GADS canonical from cloud reference run (drafted lane, TWFE DiD with state+year fixed effects, clustered SEs, poverty/unemployment/youth-demographic controls): +0.1057 homicides per 100,000, p=0.6037 — NOT statistically significant. The published finding (Cheng & Hoekstra 2013) is a significant ~8% increase. Same direction (positive) but the GADS run finds no significant effect, likely because this benchmark's CSV was deliberately trimmed from the source's 139 columns to 17 (dropping the region-by-quarter fixed effects and state-specific linear time trends the original paper's precision depends on) — see notes.md for a self-critical note on that trimming choice.
